purpose: Two small system-infrastructure blocks. neorv32_sys_reset turns one asynchronous external reset and two synchronous reset-request inputs into two reset outputs: an external-domain reset that only the external reset drives, and a system reset that the external reset or either request drives. Each is asserted at once and released synchronously after a 4-stage shift register fills, and the two requests are exported as registered copies. neorv32_sys_clock OR-reduces a vector of enable requests and, while any is set, runs a 12-bit counter whose bit rising edges become 8 one-cycle clock-enable tick outputs (periods 2 to 4096 cycles, simulated).

DERIVES_FROM sreg_ext via and_reduce_f (L52); constant '0' on reset (L46); storage edge

conceptual_assets.name: CA1 system reset state

C.why: a 1-bit level computed from a shift register that only holds shifted-in '1's or a clear (L55, L57); no secret enters.

I.why: either request input at '0' clears sreg_sys (L55) and rstn_sys_o falls on the next edge (L59); a spurious or unauthorised request resets everything this output drives, and a corrupted all-ones sreg_sys would release reset early (L59). Simulated: a 1-cycle request gives a 4-cycle reset, a 3-cycle request a 6-cycle reset.

A.why: holding either request at '0' re-clears sreg_sys every cycle (L54-55), so rstn_sys_o stays low for as long as it is held (simulated); rstn_ext_i also forces it low asynchronously (L44, L48).

U.why: the condition is a plain OR of two request inputs with no enable, lock or privilege term, so whoever drives either input can reset the system at will. That one of them comes from a debugger is suggested by its name only.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Driving rstn_wdt_i or rstn_dbg_i to '0' (L54) clears sreg_sys (L55) and pulls rstn_sys_o low from the next edge until 3 edges after the request ends (L57, L59), resetting or, if held, freezing the system domain on demand.

conceptual_assets.name: CA2 reset-request status (the two request inputs as read and exported)

I.why: the request value decides the system reset (L54-55) and leaves the module as a registered copy (L72, L73) held in the external reset domain (cleared only at L69-70, never by the system reset it causes); a corrupted request resets the system, a corrupted copy misreports the request to whatever consumes it.

A.why: nothing in this module masks or delays a request beyond one register stage: L54 acts on it unconditionally while the external reset is released, and L72-73 copy it every edge.

U.why: same override as CA1: an unqualified request input forces the system reset.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: A forged request both resets the system domain (L54-55, L59) and appears on xrstn_wdt_o or xrstn_ocd_o one edge later (L72-73), so downstream logic sees the forged request as genuine.

conceptual_assets.name: CA3 external-domain reset state

I.why: rstn_ext_o is released only when all 4 bits of sreg_ext are '1' (L51-52); a corrupted sreg_ext changes when the external domain leaves reset, and a spurious rstn_ext_i resets it (L44-46).

A.why: rstn_ext_i at '0' forces rstn_ext_o low asynchronously and holds it (L44-46); release comes on the 5th edge after rstn_ext_i returns high (simulated).

U.why: no mode or override: L51-52 contain no request term, so neither request input can reset this domain. State held under rstn_ext_o therefore survives a request-triggered system reset; that is by design here and a risk only if a security state sits in that domain (not visible; see H2).

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Pulling rstn_ext_i low (L44) clears sreg_ext and rstn_ext_o (L45-46) and also rstn_sys_o (L48), resetting both domains; both outputs return high on the 5th edge after rstn_ext_i is released (L51-52, L57, L59).

hypotheses: H1 tick time base: if a downstream timeout mechanism (for example a watchdog) counts clk_en_o ticks, corrupting cnt/cnt2 by fault injection would shift its timeout, and a requester that has just enabled gets its first tick at an arbitrary phase (up to one full period early) because cnt keeps running for other requesters (L129-135). No line in this module shows such a consumer.

H2 domain split: rstn_ext_o is not driven by either request input (no request term in L51-52; map reachability: rstn_wdt_i and rstn_dbg_i never reach sreg_ext or rstn_ext_o). Any debug-session or lock state placed in the rstn_ext_o domain would survive a request-triggered system reset. Consumers are not visible.

H3 xrstn_wdt_o and xrstn_ocd_o are not sticky (they follow the input one edge later, L72-73, simulated); if a consumer treats them as a reset-cause record, the cause is lost once the request ends. Consumers are not visible.
H4 rstn_ext_i is asynchronous with no glitch filter or minimum-width check (L44, L68): a short glitch resets both domains; physical fault-injection surface.
H5 rstn_wdt_i and rstn_dbg_i are sampled by a single flop with no synchronizer (L54, L72-73); safe only if their drivers are synchronous to clk_i, which this source does not show.
H6 the index constants clk_div2_c ... clk_div4096_c (L140-147) are in neither the map nor the source; which bit of clk_en_o carries which period is inferred from the cnt bit used, not verified.

map_assessment.used_for: Indexing all 17 elements and their 87 occurrences; building the flow graph (43 forward edges, 0 without a reverse edge); reachability showed that rstn_wdt_i and rstn_dbg_i reach only sreg_sys, rstn_sys_o and their own copies, never sreg_ext or rstn_ext_o (the domain split); the RESETS vs GATES labels separated the true process reset (rstn_ext_i) from the two synchronous request inputs, which decided the Step 5 exclusion; storage kinds (edge vs none) gave the 'stores' roles.
map_assessment.insufficient_for: Security meaning: every C/I/A/U answer came from reading the lines plus domain knowledge, not from the map. Consumers of every output: this pack has no connections, so the harm side of each integrity question stops at the port. Timing: the map cannot say that a 1-cycle request gives a 4-cycle reset or that release takes 5 edges; I simulated the lines for that. Constants: clk_div*_c indices are absent.
map_assessment.errors_found: No wrong edge found; all 87 occurrence texts match the source lines. One labelling caveat: clk_en_o GATED_BY cnt, cnt2 (L140-147) follows the single-bit-operand rule, but on the line it is the data computation of the output, so a reader following only control edges would mis-class cnt/cnt2 as influence points. Hints are accurate except 'synchronized' for xrstn_wdt_o and xrstn_ocd_o, which are single-flop samples.

process_notes: 1) Read the prompt. 2) Read the whole source (two entities, about 60 statement lines). 3) Indexed the map with a script (elements, occurrences, edges, storage). 4) Built a flow graph, checked edge symmetry and computed reachability from every input. 5) Wrote a cycle model of L42-75 and L122-147 and simulated reset timing and tick periods, because the claims about pulse widths and release latency are not in the map. 6) Answered the four questions per value with the mechanism line. 7) Assigned roles (sets/stores/exit port) from storage kind and edge direction. 8) Validated every cited occurrence id against the map and every occurrence text against the source. Where the map changed a decision: the RESETS/GATES split put rstn_ext_i under the Step 5 reset exclusion while keeping rstn_wdt_i and rstn_dbg_i as 'sets'; the missing request->sreg_ext edges established the domain split used in CA3 and H2. Where the source overrode the map: clk_en_o's GATED_BY edges are data, read on L140-147. Where the prompt pulled against judgement: the Step 5 reset rule excludes rstn_ext_i although in a reset generator the reset input is the data; and the rule 'a yes needs a line that exports the value' is met by any output, so the neorv32_sys_clock decision (not an asset) rests on judging that no harm is shown in this module, not on the absence of a line.
